```{r}


plot_shift_with_hist_qty <- function(coef_data, variables, type, matched){
  

  plot_data <- coef_data %>% 
    filter(variable %in% variables) %>% 
    mutate(estimate = ifelse(variable == "global_tilted_irradiance", estimate*10, estimate),
           pretty_variable = case_when(
      variable == "renewable_day_ahead_forecast" ~ "Renewable Day-ahead Forecast (MWh)",
      variable == "global_tilted_irradiance" ~ "Irradiance (0.1W/m2)",
      variable == "wind_speed_100m" ~ "Wind Speed (m/s)",
      variable == "unpredicted_renewables" ~ "Unpredicted Renewables (MWh)",
      variable == "intraday_update_renewables" ~ "Intraday Update Renewables (MWh)",
      variable == "cbf_es" ~ "CBF (MWh)",
      variable == "cold_excess_supply" ~ "Excess Cold (°C)",
      variable == "heat_excess_supply" ~ "Excess Heat (°C)",
      variable == "cold_excess_demand" ~ "Excess Cold (°C)",
      variable == "heat_excess_demand" ~ "Excess Heat (°C)",
      TRUE ~ variable  # fallback
    ))
  # %>% 
  #   filter(price_test >= -100)
  
  # Définir un facteur de mise à l'échelle pour que l'histogramme rentre dans l'échelle principale
  scale_factor <- max(plot_data$estimate, na.rm = TRUE) / max(hist(price_indispo_merge_esp$gen_tot_da, plot = FALSE)$counts)
  
  my_plot <- ggplot(data = plot_data) +
    # Courbe principale avec bande de confiance
    geom_line(aes(x = price_test, y = estimate, color = pretty_variable)) +
    geom_point(aes(x = price_test, y = estimate, color = pretty_variable)) +
    geom_line(aes(x = price_test, y = 0), linetype = "dashed")+
    geom_ribbon(
      aes(
        x = price_test, 
        ymin = estimate - 1.96 * std_error, 
        ymax = estimate + 1.96 * std_error,
        fill = pretty_variable
      ), 
      alpha = 0.2
    ) + 
    labs(
      title = paste0("Shift in ", type, " Curve"),
      x = "Price (€)",
      y = "Cumulative Energy (MWh)",
      color = "Variable",
      fill = "Variable"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

  if (matched == "matched"){
    # Définir un facteur de mise à l'échelle pour que l'histogramme rentre dans l'échelle principale
    scale_factor <- max(plot_data$estimate, na.rm = TRUE) / max(hist(price_indispo_merge_esp$price, plot = FALSE)$counts)
  
    my_plot <- my_plot + 
    # Histogramme mis à l'échelle
    geom_histogram(
      data = price_indispo_merge_esp,
      mapping = aes( x = price,  y = ..count.. * scale_factor),
      bins = 60,
      color = "black",
      fill = NA
    )
    
    # Axe secondaire
    # scale_y_continuous(
    #   name = "Price (€/GWh)",
    #   sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / scale_factor, name = "Fréquence de gen_tot")
    # )
  }
  my_plot <- my_plot +
  coord_flip(xlim = c(-20, 180))

  return(my_plot)
}

```
